Soil Liquefaction - The Evidence

In June 2011, Christchurch, New Zealand suffered an earthquake that left a lot of the city in chaos, destroying buildings and infrastructure and leaving over 50,000 homes without power. As a result, there were collapsed houses, ruptured water mains, flooding, and fires due to disrupted electrical lines. Due to the strong ground motions and intense shaking, part of the city experienced a strange phenomenon known as soil liquefaction. Sand boils emerged from asphalt roads, toppling and sinking cars and causing boulders to fall from hills, resulting in more home damage.

Soil liquefaction occurs when saturated soil loses its strength and stiffness in response to an applied stress such as shaking or other sudden changes such as a strong explosion. Loose, saturated soil or sand has a tendency to compress when a load is applied, but in the event of a stress such as shaking or an explosion, we see the opposite. The soil tends to dilate, and the result is treacherous quicksand or quick clay. The land turns to liquid, causing structures of heavy mass such as buildings, infrastructure, and cars to start sinking, toppling over, or collapsing. It can also affect dams and bridges. Turbidity currents can also form huge landslides that are impossible to stop. In the worst-case scenario, entire cities may be destroyed.

As you can see, liquefaction can move entire areas of land. The mud can rise dramatically and rapidly, and its destructive force is unstoppable. It is a well-documented phenomenon.

The 1964 earthquake in Niigata, Japan caused liquefaction, and we can see the effects very clearly in photos—the same with the 1964 Alaska earthquake. Buildings toppling, cars sinking, infrastructure collapsing. Once the stress has subsided, the soil begins to solidify once again, and we can see the aftermath: uneven, muddy streets remain where there was once road paving.

Returning to photographs of 19th century cities, we see a similar situation. The roads are unrefined and full of mud. We see unsophisticated, uneven, coarse, and muddy roads everywhere against a backdrop of refined, sophisticated, and magnificent architecture.

Could these cities have suffered a similar fate of soil liquefaction that we see in more recent times? Perhaps. But unfortunately, muddy roads are not enough evidence to base any conclusions on, is it?

The Legend of Saint Christopher

As the legend goes, Opherus was a strong giant but with a dull mind. His intentions were always good. He wanted to serve the most powerful king on Earth. He was sent to the court of a mighty king to serve him. One day, the king, hearing a singer say the devil's name, made a sign of the cross with terror.

"Why do you make that sign?" Opherus asked.

"Because I fear the devil," the king replied.

"If you fear him, you are not as powerful as him," Opherus reasoned. "I want to serve the devil."

And so he did. He enrolled among Satan's servants. One day, the servants met a cross by the side of the road, and the devil ordered them to turn around.

"Why is that?" the curious Opherus asked.

"Because I fear the image of Christ," the devil replied.

"If you fear him, you are not as powerful as him," Opherus reasoned. "I want to enter the service of Christ."

Opherus exclaimed and passed by the cross and went on his way. On his way, Opherus met a hermit. He asked the hermit where he could find Christ.

"Everywhere," the hermit replied.

The hermit knew the type of dull giant he was dealing with, and he knew he would not take to prayer. So he led Opherus to a violent river and said: "The poor people who have crossed this water have drowned. Stay here and carry them on your strong shoulders. If you do this, Christ will recognize you as his servant."

And so he did. Opherus spent his days and nights carrying people across the river.

One night, overwhelmed with fatigue, Opherus received a knock on his door. It was a child who wanted to cross. Opherus took him on his shoulders and began crossing the river. But as he reached the middle, the river became a furious torrent. The waves swelled, and Opherus began to buckle. In fear of letting the child fall, Opherus uprooted a tree to lean on. But the child was becoming heavier and heavier. Opherus began to fear the child would drown. He lifted his head up and asked:

"Child, why do you make yourself so heavy? It seems to me that I carry the world."

The child replied: "Not only do you carry the world, you carry the one that made the world. I am Christ. As a reward, I baptize you in the name of the Father, in my own name, and in the name of the Holy Spirit. From now on, you will be called Christopher."

The Sun's Journey

We live on a flat plain. Our world is an electromagnetic terrarium surrounded by an ethereal sea of water. Like all terrariums, after initial creation, it begins to form its own self-sustaining atmosphere.

The sun and the moon journey above our flat realm in concentric spirals. There are five prominent circles of latitude. We are told we have:
- The Arctic Circle (closest to the center)
- The Tropic of Cancer (at 23.5 degrees latitude in the northern hemisphere)
- The Equator (at zero degree latitude)
- The Tropic of Capricorn (at 23.5 degrees latitude in the southern hemisphere)
- The Antarctic Circle

The sun journeys from the equator at the March equinox up in concentric spirals to the Tropic of Cancer. When the sun is in this position, the northern hemisphere experiences summer and the southern hemisphere experiences winter. After which, the sun turns and begins making its way back to the equator.

The word "tropic" stems from the Latin word tropicus, which means "pertaining to a turn."

The sun journeys back, taking the same concentric spiral path, and reaches the equator again. It then keeps going and reaches the Tropic of Capricorn. When the sun is in this position, the southern hemisphere experiences summer and the northern hemisphere experiences winter. After a time, the sun turns and begins making its way back to the equator for the March equinox.

The equinox occurs when the sun is journeying on the circle of the equator, and those living along this line of latitude will see the sun directly overhead at a 90-degree angle at solar noon.

The March equinox marks a season of spring in the northern hemisphere and autumn in the southern hemisphere. The September equinox marks autumn in the northern hemisphere and spring in the southern hemisphere.

It is important to note that the sun never reaches the Arctic Circle, nor does it reach the Antarctic Circle. It never reaches the poles. It journeys to the tropic circles and then turns back.

The point at which the sun reaches its most northerly and southerly excursion relative to the equator is called the solstice. "Solstice" comes from the Latin word solstitium, which means "point at which the sun seems to stand still." Indeed, many do note that the sun seems to stop on the solstices. This is because, in a sense, it does. It reaches the most northerly and southerly excursion and turns back.

Soil Liquefaction - The Evidence

In June 2011, Christchurch, New Zealand suffered an earthquake that left a lot of the city in chaos, destroying buildings and infrastructure and leaving over 50,000 homes without power. As a result, there were collapsed houses, ruptured water mains, flooding, and fires due to disrupted electrical lines. Due to the strong ground motions and intense shaking, part of the city experienced a strange phenomenon known as soil liquefaction. Sand boils emerged from asphalt roads, toppling and sinking cars and causing boulders to fall from hills, resulting in more home damage.

Soil liquefaction occurs when saturated soil loses its strength and stiffness in response to an applied stress such as shaking or other sudden changes such as a strong explosion. Loose, saturated soil or sand has a tendency to compress when a load is applied, but in the event of a stress such as shaking or an explosion, we see the opposite. The soil tends to dilate, and the result is treacherous quicksand or quick clay. The land turns to liquid, causing structures of heavy mass such as buildings, infrastructure, and cars to start sinking, toppling over, or collapsing. It can also affect dams and bridges. Turbidity currents can also form huge landslides that are impossible to stop. In the worst-case scenario, entire cities may be destroyed.

As you can see, liquefaction can move entire areas of land. The mud can rise dramatically and rapidly, and its destructive force is unstoppable. It is a well-documented phenomenon.

The 1964 earthquake in Niigata, Japan caused liquefaction, and we can see the effects very clearly in photos—the same with the 1964 Alaska earthquake. Buildings toppling, cars sinking, infrastructure collapsing. Once the stress has subsided, the soil begins to solidify once again, and we can see the aftermath: uneven, muddy streets remain where there was once road paving.

Returning to photographs of 19th century cities, we see a similar situation. The roads are unrefined and full of mud. We see unsophisticated, uneven, coarse, and muddy roads everywhere against a backdrop of refined, sophisticated, and magnificent architecture.

Could these cities have suffered a similar fate of soil liquefaction that we see in more recent times? Perhaps. But unfortunately, muddy roads are not enough evidence to base any conclusions on, is it?

The Legend of Saint Christopher

As the legend goes, Opherus was a strong giant but with a dull mind. His intentions were always good. He wanted to serve the most powerful king on Earth. He was sent to the court of a mighty king to serve him. One day, the king, hearing a singer say the devil's name, made a sign of the cross with terror.

"Because I fear the devil," the king replied.

"If you fear him, you are not as powerful as him," Opherus reasoned. "I want to serve the devil."

And so he did. He enrolled among Satan's servants. One day, the servants met a cross by the side of the road, and the devil ordered them to turn around.

"Why is that?" the curious Opherus asked.

"Because I fear the image of Christ," the devil replied.

"If you fear him, you are not as powerful as him," Opherus reasoned. "I want to enter the service of Christ."

Opherus exclaimed and passed by the cross and went on his way. On his way, Opherus met a hermit. He asked the hermit where he could find Christ.

"Everywhere," the hermit replied.

The hermit knew the type of dull giant he was dealing with, and he knew he would not take to prayer. So he led Opherus to a violent river and said: "The poor people who have crossed this water have drowned. Stay here and carry them on your strong shoulders. - The Equator (at zero degree latitude)
- The Tropic of Capricorn (at 23.5 degrees latitude in the southern hemisphere)
- The Antarctic Circle

The sun journeys from the equator at the March equinox up in concentric spirals to the Tropic of Cancer. When the sun is in this position, the northern hemisphere experiences summer and the southern hemisphere experiences winter. After which, the sun turns and begins making its way back to the equator.

The word "tropic" stems from the Latin word tropicus, which means "pertaining to a turn."

The sun journeys back, taking the same concentric spiral path, and reaches the equator again. It then keeps going and reaches the Tropic of Capricorn. When the sun is in this position, the southern hemisphere experiences summer and the northern hemisphere experiences winter. After a time, the sun turns and begins making its way back to the equator for the March equinox.

The equinox occurs when the sun is journeying on the circle of the equator, and those living along this line of latitude will see the sun directly overhead at a 90-degree angle at solar noon.

The March equinox marks a season of spring in the northern hemisphere and autumn in the southern hemisphere. The September equinox marks autumn in the northern hemisphere and spring in the southern hemisphere.

It is important to note that the sun never reaches the Arctic Circle, nor does it reach the Antarctic Circle. It never reaches the poles. It journeys to the tropic circles and then turns back.

The point at which the sun reaches its most northerly and southerly excursion relative to the equator is called the solstice. "Solstice" comes from the Latin word solstitium, which means "point at which the sun seems to stand still." Indeed, many do note that the sun seems to stop on the solstices. This is because, in a sense, it does. It reaches the most northerly and southerly excursion and turns back.

It will NOT involve "aliens" or "holograms" or "ascended masters." 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17 - "For the Lord himself will come down from heaven, with a loud command, with the voice of the archangel and with the trumpet call of God, and the dead in Christ will rise first. After that, we who are still alive and are left will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air." With a LOUD COMMAND. With the VOICE OF THE ARCHANGEL. With the TRUMPET OF GOD. Not subtle. Not confusing. Not "spiritual" or "metaphorical." REAL. VISIBLE. UNDENIABLE. If you see a "rapture" that involves holograms... if you hear a "message" that comes through V2K... if you witness "miracles" that look more like technology than divine power... RUN. ---

THE REMNANT - THE ONES WHO WILL NOT BOW Throughout history, God has preserved a remnant. A small group. A faithful few. Who refuse to worship the false gods. Who refuse to bow to the earthly powers. Who refuse to accept the lies. Elijah thought he was alone. "I am the only one left." God said, "I have reserved seven thousand who have not bowed the knee to Baal" (1 Kings 19:18). The same is true today. You are not alone. There are others. All over the world. In every nation. In every church. In every "conspiracy" forum. People who SEE. People who KNOW. People who are PREPARING. The remnant will: - Refuse the mark (whatever it costs) - Refuse the one world religion (even if it means death) - Refuse the Antichrist (even when he seems "good") - Refuse to be silent (even when speaking means persecution) - Refuse to be afraid (even when the whole world is terrified) The remnant will: - Trust God (not the government, not the media, not the "experts") - Love each other (true community, true fellowship, true sacrifice) - Bear witness (to the truth, to the gospel, to Christ) - Endure to the end (not "escape," but ENDURE) Matthew 24:13 - "But the one who stands firm to the end will be saved." Not "the one who is raptured." Not "the one who escapes." "The one who STANDS FIRM to the end." Be part of the remnant. ---

THE PREPARATION - WHAT YOU NEED TO DO You've read this far. You know what's coming. Now what?

SPIRITUAL PREPARATION 1. Get right with God. Not religious. Not "spiritual." Not "I believe in something." REPENT. Confess your sins. Turn from your wicked ways. Surrender to Christ. 2. Get in the Word. The Bible is your weapon. Your shield. Your guide. Read it. Study it. MEMORIZE it. When the deception comes, you will NEED the truth in your heart. 3. Get in community. You cannot do this alone. Find others who see the truth. Meet together. Pray together. Prepare together. The remnant is not individuals. It's a BODY. 4. Get on your knees. Prayer is your connection to the throne. Your lifeline to heaven. Your source of strength. Pray without ceasing.

PRACTICAL PREPARATION 1. Get out of debt. The system will collapse. Currencies will fail. Banks will close. Owning debt means owning OBLIGATION to the system. Free yourself. 2. Get food. Store what you can. Learn to grow. Learn to preserve. Learn to hunt. The supply chains will not hold. 3. Get water. Filtration. Collection. Storage. Water is life. Without it, you have days. 4. Get skills. Can you garden? Can you build? Can you heal? Can you defend? The "economy" will not provide. You must provide for yourself and your community. 5. Get off the grid. Digital ID is coming. Social credit is coming. The mark is coming. The less you depend on the system, the easier it will be to refuse it. 6. Get together. Form communities. Share resources. Build networks. The remnant will survive together or die separately.

MENTAL PREPARATION 1. Accept the cost. You may lose everything. Your job. Your home. Your family. Your friends. Your freedom. Your LIFE. Accept it now, or you will not survive when it happens. 2. Reject the fear. Fear is the enemy's weapon. Do not be afraid. Not of the virus. Not of the vaccine. Not of the mark. Not of death. Fear God, and you will fear nothing else. 3. Embrace the truth. Truth is not "what works." Truth is not "what feels good." Truth is not "what the experts say." Truth is what GOD says. Embrace it. Live it. Die for it. 4. Love the martyrs. Those who have gone before. Who refused to bow. Who chose death over denial. They are your CLOUD OF WITNESSES (Hebrews 12:1). Follow their example. 5. Fix your eyes on Jesus. Not on the Antichrist. Not on the Tribulation. Not on the "aliens." On JESUS. The author and perfecter of your faith (Hebrews 12:2). ---

THE HOPE - WHY YOU CAN FACE THIS This chapter has been dark. I know. Apocalyptic. Terrifying. But I haven't told you the whole truth. The whole truth is that GOD WINS. Revelation 19:11-16 - "I saw heaven standing open and there before me was a white horse, whose rider is called Faithful and True. With justice he judges and wages war... On his robe and on his thigh he has this name written: KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS." Jesus returns. Not as a hologram. Not as a "alien." Not as a "ascended master." As KING. As LORD. As JUDGE. The Antichrist will be defeated. The false prophet will be thrown alive into the lake of fire. The beast will be destroyed. Revelation 20:10 - "And the devil, who deceived them, was thrown into the lake of burning sulfur, where the beast and the false prophet had been thrown. They will be tormented day and night for ever and ever." Forever. Not temporary. Not "rehabilitation." ETERNAL punishment. Revelation 21:1-4 - "Then I saw 'a new heaven and a new earth,' for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away... 'He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the old order of things has passed away.'" No more death. No more pain. No more tears. No more good called evil. No more evil called good. The inversion will be REVERSED. The light will overcome the darkness. The truth will prevail. And YOU—if you endure to the end—will be there. ---

THE INVITATION You've read three chapters of this book. You've seen the evidence. You've heard the warnings. You know what's coming. Now you have a choice. Reject the truth. Go back to sleep. Pretend you didn't read this. Scroll through your phone. Watch your shows. Live your "normal" life. And face the Tribulation UNPREPARED. Or ACCEPT the truth. Wake up. Stay awake. Prepare yourself. Prepare your family. Prepare your community. Face the Tribulation with your EYES OPEN and your HOPE FIRM. The choice is yours. But know this: The time is SHORT. The deception is ALREADY HERE. The reset is ALREADY BEGINNING. Do not wait. Tomorrow may be too late. Romans 13:11 - "And do this, understanding the present time: The hour has already come for you to wake up from your slumber, because our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed." Wake up. ---

THE PRAYER FOR THE REMNANT If you have read this far, and you believe what you've read, and you want to be part of the remnant, pray this prayer. Father, I have seen the deception. I know what's coming. I choose to wake up. Forgive me for my sins. Forgive me for sleeping. Forgive me for ignoring the warnings. I surrender my life to you. My future to you. My fears to you. My family to you. I refuse the mark of the beast. I refuse the one world religion. I refuse the Antichrist. I refuse the "aliens." I refuse every counterfeit. I choose the truth. I choose the cross. I choose the blood. I choose the name of Jesus. Prepare me for what's coming. Give me courage when I am afraid. Give me strength when I am weak. Give me wisdom when I am confused. Surround me with the remnant. Help us to stand together. To pray together. To prepare together. And when the Tribulation comes—when the world turns against us—when the mark is enforced—when the beasts rise—give us grace to endure. Not to escape. To ENDURE. To the end. In Jesus' name. Amen. --- End of Chapter 5 This is not the end of the book. But it may be the end of your comfort. What you do with what you've learned is between you and God. Choose wisely. ---✝️ Keep Jesus in your heart ✝️
